newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories up slightly in February.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories up slightly in February.

text.p: Businesses increased their stocks of unsold goods modestly in February, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, as booming sales pointed to steady expansion in the economy's manufacturing sector.
Total business inventories rose 0.3 percent to a seasonally adjusted $1.02 trillion after a revised 0.4 percent rise in January, the department said.

Sales kept rising briskly, up 1.4 percent to $746.27 billion in February after a 1.2 percent January rise. The February sales jump was the strongest for any month since April 1996, when they also increased 1.4 percent, Commerce said.

The brisk sales pace pulled the inventory-to-sales ratio -- a measure of how long it would take to deplete stocks at the current sales pace -- to a record low of 1.36 months' worth in February from 1.38 months' in January.

"That is certainly a good sign for production," said economist Cythia Latta of DRI/McGraw Hill Inc. in Lexington, Mass. "It says that inventories are well under control, maybe even lower than desired."

Lean inventories leave room for U.S. factories to keep production rates high, which in turn means more jobs and rising incomes, though some of the demand represented by vigorous sales may be met by imported goods.
Latta said she estimated gross domestic product, which measures total national output of goods and services, likely expanded at about a 4 percent annual rate in the first quarter that ended March 31.

Federal Reserve policy-makers, who raised short-term interest rates on March 25 to dampen demand, would prefer an economic growth rate nearer 2 percent to 2-1/4 percent in order to head off a potential inflationary flareup in prices and wage demands.
"These (inventory) figures suggest that we may have entered the second quarter with considerable momentum," Latta said.
Previously, the department said that January inventories had risen by 0.1 percent but it revised that estimate upward.
In February, inventories increased at both the manufacturers' and retailers' levels, but they were unchanged from January at wholesalers.

Retail inventories rose 0.5 percent in February to $314.99 billion and manufacturers' inventories were up 0.4 percent to $441.76 billion. Wholesalers' inventories were flat in February at $260.05 billion.
At auto dealerships, inventories rose 0.5 percent in February to $88.17 billion.
